Commentary.Commentary: Now then, the total is a competitive one but the wicket seems quite flat. New Zealand will have to bat well, they will be looking to get a lead as it is them who will be batting last so a lead will be very important. England on the other hand, will be also be eager to get any sort of a lead as it could prove to be very handy. Stay tuned to find out how the Kiwis go along with the bat.

The New Zealand bowling wasn't great to begin with on both the days. However, they kept getting better as the day progressed. Boult though was disappointing, he finished with just the one wicket and was also quite wayward. Had he bowled better, England might have not even scored 300. Southee was the pick as he finished with a four-fer. Could have and should have had a fifer but Raval dropped Buttler off his bowling. Wagner and Colin de Grandhomme also impressed with 3 and 2 each respectively.

England though will be mighty disappointed! They just threw away all the hard work done by them on Day 1. After electing to bat, they showed grit and determination to battle it out against a disciplined bowling attack yesterday. Fifties from Denly, Burns and Stokes saw England end the day at 241 for 4. They entered Day 2 with a positive approach with Pope and Stokes adding some quick runs before the left-hander was dismissed in the nervous 90s. That started the procession. The visitors then slipped to 295 for 8 and 350 also looked farfetched. Buttler though manage to play a crucial innings, he was well-supported by Leach who once again showed he is capable enough to hang in there. The two added 52 and took England close to 350. The last pair could not make an impact but ensured the away side did cross the 350-run mark.

So England just about manage to cross the 350-run mark before being bundled up! The Kiwi openers rush off the field to pad up and Broad too is seen running towards the pavilion as he needs to get ready to do his job with the ball. Warm applause now as the Kiwi players make their way out, they have to be pleased with their comeback today. At one stage it seemed England are all set for a big first innings score but the Kiwis have managed to pull it back brilliantly and the game is evenly poised at the moment.

OUT! CASTLED! Finally England have been bowled out. Broad is the last man dismissed. Wagner sets up this wicket to perfection. He keeps on peppering Broad with short stuff and surprises him with a full ball. Broad is stuck on the back foot as he looks to push this full ball through the off side. The ball takes the inside edge and goes onto disturb the furniture behind. ENGLAND END ON 353!
Good length and on middle, Broad plays it to mid-wicket.
Length and on off, Broad defends it to the off side.
Three in a row and Broad is been tested with some short stuff. Wagner once again goes short and Stuart  plays it towards fine leg.
Another short one and on the body, Broad defends it awkwardly towards fine leg for no run.
Back of a length and on off, Broad hops as he defends, the ball goes uppishly towards mid on but falls just in front of the fielder.
Outside off, left alone.
Another delivery on a good length, Leach stays back and keeps it out.
Good length and on off, Leach guides it to the man at point.
Outside off, it is left alone.
Shorter and outside off, this is guided through point for one.
Beaten all ends up! This is on off and it is on a length. Goes away with the angle. Southee defends inside the line and gets beaten.
Fuller one on pads, Leach flicks it to mid-wicket.
On a length and down the leg side, Leach looks to flick it off his pads but fails to lay bat on ball.
FOUR! Deliberately done by Broad. Wagner bowls a length ball outside off and Stuart plays it with an open face and gets it to the third man fence for a boundary.
Short one and on middle, Broad ducks and the ball goes over him to the keeper. Watling there fails to grab it cleanly. The ball goes towards fine leg and the batsmen steal a bye.
Fuller one on the pads, Broad drives it to mid on.
Stuart Broad, the last man walks out to bat.

OUT! Straight to the man! Raval will be a relieved man! The dropped catch in the last over does not cost a lot. End of a frustrating stand for everyone except for England. Also, a handy innings from Buttler comes to an end. With him not taking the singles, boundaries are what he was looking for. He tried to hit one here too. A short ball outside off, Buttler cuts it hard but does so uppishly. It does not have the distance in it and it goes straight to Santner at deep point who takes it easily. Actually, Buttler might not have spotted a deep point as Santner was signing autographs before Wagner ran in and then rushed onto the field when he saw Wagner getting close to deliver the ball. Jos might not have played that shot had he seen Santner there.
Slower one and way wide outside off. It goes further away and wide signalled by the umpire.
Buttler keeps strike now as he guides it through point for one.

FOUR! Frustrating this for the Kiwis! A dropped catch earlier in the over and now a boundary. Shorter and outside off, Buttler slaps it through covers and it races away. England nearing in on the 350-run mark.
Another couple! Shorter and outside off, Buttler cuts it behind point and two is taken.
Fuller and on off, Buttler pushes it to covers.

In the air... this should be the end of Buttler, this should be Southee's fifer but Raval spills it. Southee is frustrated and rightly so. He bowls a off cutter outside off, Buttler looks to go big but ends up slicing it towards cover. Raval runs in from the deep, Nicholls also thinks of going after it from covers but then stops. Raval then looks to take it with a dive forward but puts it down. Maybe that moment of confusion whether it is he who is going to catch or Nicholls, cost him. Two taken by the batters. This could prove very costly.
Shorter and on off, Buttler pulls it through square leg but no runs taken again.
Buttler gets the single on the last ball! It is very full and outside off, Buttler squirts it wide of deep point for one.
A slower one on off, Buttler smashes it to long off for no runs.
One more short ball on off, Buttler pulls it through mid-wicket but once again, no runs taken. The fielder now comes in.
Buttler clears his front leg and Wagner bowls it way too wide outside off. Buttler looks to go after it but misses.
Another short one outside off, Buttler pulls it again through square leg but does not run.
Pulled hard but for no runs! Shorter and outside off, Buttler hammers it but on the bounce to the fielder at deep square leg. Does not run.
Length and around off, Leach Shoulders arms to it.
Good length and outside off, Buttler cuts it through point for a run.
Short and Wide outside off, Buttler rides the bounce and pulls it to mid-wicket.
Fuller one on the pads, Leach flicks it towards fine leg and gets off strike.
Short ball down the leg side, Leach ducks under it with ease.
Length and on off, Leach defends it to covers.
Length delivery on off, Buttler mistimes it to cover. A dot to end which means once again Leach will face the start of next over.
A couple now! Good fielding! A full toss outside off, Buttler puts bat to ball and gets it through covers. Santner in the deep runs to his right, dives and keeps it down to two.
Fuller and on off, this is hit to the man at covers.
Outside off, this is not played at.
A slower one outside off, Buttler does not fiddle with it.
A single on the first ball which means Buttler is back on strike! Shorter and on the body, Leach looks to flick but misses. It hits the pads and rolls towards fine leg. A leg bye taken.
Neil Wagner to bowl from the other end.
Length and outside off, Leach drives it to covers and retains the strike. Good start to the session.
Length and outside off, Leach blocks it to the off side.
Full and outside off, Buttler drives it to long on and gets Leach on strike for the next ball.
Good length but down the leg side, Buttler looks to flick but fails to lay bat on ball.
Length and on off, Buttler drives it to mid off.
Length and outside off, Buttler is happy let that go.

Welcome back for the post lunch session. The Kiwi players are out in the middle taking their respective fielding positions. Out walk the two England batsmen, Jos Buttler and Jack Leach. New Zealand would want to end the England innings quickly by taking the remaining two wickets. Whereas, England would hope that this pair of Buttler and Leach bats longer and grind out some useful runs. Tim Southee to start the session with the ball. Here we go...
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

An excellent session for the hosts! 4 wickets in this session means they are right back into the game. However, it did not start all that well for them. They were leaking runs at the start with Stokes and Pope scoring at will. It seemed that England are all set for something around 400 or even more but then came the collapse. A stunning catch by Taylor to dismiss Stokes opened the floodgates. They lost 4 wickets for 18 runs with Southee picking up three and Boult taking one. Buttler and Leach though are doing really well here. They are amidst a 34-run stand and England would want the two to continue. New Zealand on the other hand, will hope to get the remaining two as quickly as possible. Join us for the second session in a while.
Tossed up and around off, Leach keeps it out. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 2.
Short and wide outside off, Leach cuts it to point.
Tossed up on middle and leg, Leach drives it back to the bowler.
Fuller one on the pads, Leach works it to square leg.
Fuller one outside off, Leach blocks it to the off side.
Tossed up outside off, Leach defends it off the front foot and into the ground.
Mitchell Santner comes on to bowl just before lunch.
A dot to end! Shorter and on off, this is pushed to the man at mid off.
On the shorter side around off, Buttler stands tall and guides it to point.
WIDE! Way too short and down the leg side. It has been wided for height.
SIX! Dispatched! That is some hit by Buttler. This is a length delivery on off, Buttler lofts it with ease over the long off fence for a biggie.
On the shorter side, Buttler does well to pull it along the ground through square leg but once again does not take the run.
Back of a length on off, Buttler pushes it towards cover where the fielder makes a good stop.
Good length and on off, Buttler pushes it to mid off.
Once again the single is refused on the last ball! Shorter and on the body, this is worked down towards fine leg.
A short one but slides it down the leg side, Leach lets it be.
Outside edge but for one! Full and wide outside off, Buttler goes after it. It goes off the outside edge down to third man for one.
One more short ball outside off, Buttler looks to drag it through the leg side but it goes off the underedge and on the bounce to the keeper.
A short one on middle, Buttler ducks under it.
Full and outside off, Buttler is once again guilty of going too hard at the ball, it goes off the inner half back to the bowler.
Well bowled! An inswinging yorker from Boult on off. Leach does well to jam it out.
Shorter in length and outside off, Leach cuts it but finds point.
Back of a length and on middle, this is pushed down to long on for one.
A sharp short one. Buttler initially looks to pull but then realizes it is too quick and bails out.
Fuller and on off, Buttler strokes it to mid off who is right at the edge of the circle.
From around the wicket, this is angled into the off pole. Defended.
Trent Boult is back on. 29-6-89-1 are his figures so far. Can he break the Leach resistance and finish things off for New Zealand with the ball?
Nicely played but no runs taken! Shorter and on the body, Leach works it towards fine leg but Buttler does not take the single.
Fuller and on off, Buttler creams it through covers but just for one.
Outside off, not played at.
The knuckle ball but it is outside off, Buttler lets it be.
Outside off, left alone.
Length delivery and around off, Buttler guides it towards gully where the fielder makes a good stop diving to his right.
Two to end the over! Length delivery and outside off, Leach opens the face of the bat and plays it down towards third man for two.
Back of a length and on off, Leach pushes it to mid off.
Back of a length and on off, this is pushed through covers for one.
In the air... safe! Shorter and on middle, Buttler is early in the pull shot. It goes off the arm and lobs on the off side.
On the stumps, this is kept out.
Outside off, left alone.
WIDE! Bangs this one way too short and on middle, goes above the head of Buttler. Wided.
Colin de Grandhomme is back! 22-5-37-2 are his figures so far.
Another short one and Leach negotiates it well by evading it. A over full of short balls which was played out with ease by Leach.
Once again it is a bumper, Leach defends it onto the ground with utmost ease.
Bangs this one in again, Leach defends it out confidently.
Shortish and on middle, Leach stands tall and works it to mid-wicket.
Shorter again and on middle, Leach works it to mid-wicket.
That is a sharp bumper and well directed too. Leach does well to evade it.
Good stop! Fuller and outside off, Leach drives it towards cover. The fielder there dives and stops it partially. Saves three for his side. Also, that stop means, Leach will continue to be on strike.
Well bowled and well played! A yorker right on middle, Leach gets his bat down in time and keeps it out.
One more ball on a good length and around off, Leach keeps it out nicely.
Outside off, it is left alone.
Good length and on off from over the wicket. It is defended onto the ground.
This is angled into the pads, Leach works it to mid-wicket.
Wagner bowls one down the leg and Buttler looks to paddle it fine but fails to get wood on the ball. Watling behind the wickets dives to his left and takes it.
BEATEN! Wide and outside off, Buttler looks to go downtown but is nowhere near the ball as the ball goes past the outside edge.
Length and outside off, A bit off extra bounce too. Buttler slaps it to covers.
Fuller and on the pads, Leach flicks it through square leg. Till the ball gets fielded in the deep, the batsmen take a comfortable three.
Short ball on middle, Leach does well to drop his wrists and evade it.
Length and outside off, Leach defends it to point.
FOUR! Width on offer and Buttler makes Southee pay. This is wide outside off, Buttler just guides it past point and bags a boundary. An expensive over this.
From around the wicket Southee bowls a big inswinger but it ends up on the pads. Leach looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. It rolls towards fine leg. A leg bye taken.
On the shorter side, this is pulled through square leg for one.
Slightly shorter and on off, this is defended.

FOUR! Up and over! Buttler can be very dangerous if gets going. He is looking for the boundaries right now and that shot makes that evident. This is fuller and on middle, Jos lofts it over the mid on fielder for a boundary.
Good length and closer to the off pole, Buttler goes hard at it but it goes off the inner half back to the bowler.
Wat too wide outside off, it is left alone.
Shorter and outside off, Leach goes after it but misses.
Back of a length and on off, Leach is solid in defense.
Way too wide outside off to make the batter play.
Down the leg side, Leach looks to flick but misses.
Outside off, Leach lets it be.
Neil Wagner is on now!
Back of a length on off, this is defended onto the ground.
On the pads, this is worked down to fine leg for one.
Outside off, left alone.
A short one on the body, Leach ducks under it.
Drags his length back and bowls it outside off, Leach lets it be.

FOUR! 300 up for England! Fuller and outside off, Leach leans into it and strokes it through covers. Williamson from extra cover gives it a chase and tries to stop it but the ball touches the ropes first.
Good length and around off, Buttler defends it off the back foot.
Length and around off, Buttler defends it to the off side.

RUN OUT CHANCE MISSED! A dirict hit and Buttler was a gonner. Boult bowls a wide yorker and Leach just squeezes it to point and calls for a run. Henry Nicholls there grabs the ball but fails to hit the stumps at the striker's end. In the end the Batsmen take an easy single.
Jack Leach is the new man in. He needs to stay out there with Buttler. He does have the pedigree to do so.

OUT! CAUGHT! New Zealand are on fire. Boult gets his revenge. He bowls one on  a length gets it across the right hander. Archer pokes at it as he is rooted to his crease. The ball takes the outside edge and goes low towards second slip. Tim Southee there dives low and takes a brillant catch. You just cannot keep Southee out off the game. First with the ball and now in the field. England losing the ploy here.

FOUR! A committed effort in the field from Santner. Boult bowls a fuller one and wide outside off, Archer just opens the face off the bat at the last moment and steers it through point. Mitchell Santner runs behind the ball from covers and puts in a dive but fails to keep the ball in play. A boundary to get off the mark for Archer.
Fuller in length and on the pads, Buttler flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR LEG BYES! No hat-trick! Not the best of balls too. This is on the pads, Archer looks to flick but misses. It hits the pad and goes past the diving keeper and into the fine leg fence. End of a tremendous over by Southee.
Jofra Archer walks out to bat. He will face the Hat-Trick ball from Southee. Four slips, a gully and a leg gully in place.

OUT! Curran is a dead duck! Three reds and he has to take the long walk back, he takes a review along with him. Also, it is a first-baller which means Southee will be on a hat-trick. A good first delivery by Southee. It starts on off and it is slightly fuller. It tails back in late. Curran fails to get his front pad out of the way as he tries to flick and the ball hits that pad. An appeal and up goes the finger. Curran reviews but it is more in hope. Replays roll in and it shows the on-field call stays. From 277 for 4, England are now 286 for 7. New Zealand right back in this now. Can they keep England under 300?
DRINKS BREAK!
Curran is a goner! He has been given LBW but he reviews. Looks plumb.
Sam Curran walks out to bat. Two new batsmen at the crease for England and an opening for New Zealand. Can the Kiwis capitalize on it?

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Another one bites the dust! The two set batters are out of here now. Poor, poor shot this by Pope. This is a sucker ball by Southee, it is full and wide outside off. Pope could have easily left that but is tempted, he tries to reach it but the ball takes a thick outside edge and goes to the right of Watling who makes no mistake. New Zealand fighting back here today morning with two early wickets. Pope walks back after getting off to a start. He shakes his head while walking back and rightly so. That is not a shot he should be proud about. Southee gets his third.
Fuller and outside off, it is left alone.
Another one on a good length, Pope keeps it out.
Back of a length and on off, Pope keeps it out.

FOUR MORE! This time edgy! This is just ahead of a length around off. Buttler is rooted to his crease as he tries to defend. Due to the angle, it goes off the outside edge, through the gap between gully and second slip and into the third man fence.
Outside off again, it is left alone.
Angles this one away from outside off, Buttler leaves it. Boult does not seem at his best in this innings so far.
FOUR! That has raced away to the fence! Boult goes fuller and gets it to tail back in from middle. Buttler gets his front leg out of the way and clips it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Outside off again, Buttler does not fiddle with it.
Outside off, left alone.
Buttler is underway! A little too straight, it is clipped through mid-wicket for one. End of a successful over from Tim Southee.
Outside off, left alone.
Back of a length and on off, Jos stands tall and keeps it out.
Back of a length and on off, Buttler is solid in defense.
Outside off, it is left alone.
Jos Buttler walks out to replace Ben Stokes in the middle.

OUT! EDGED AND THAT IS A STUNNER BY TAYLOR! WOW! He dropped a dolly yesterday but has taken an absolute blinder! Heartbreak for Ben Stokes as he falls nine short of a ton. Also, a much-needed wicket for the hosts as this partnership had started to flourish. Southee is the one who gets Big Ben. It is full and outside off, Stokes takes a few steps out and then throws his bat at it away from his body. It flies off the outside edge to the right of Taylor at widish first slip who dives with his right hand stretched out and the ball sticks. Something special was needed to get rid of Stokes and Taylor provides it. New Zealand will hope this opens the floodgates now.
On a length again, Pope plays it late and to point.
Shorter and on off, Pope stands tall and pushes it to covers.
One more ball on a good length, it is kept out.
Back of a length and on off, this is kept out.
Stokes takes a few steps down the track and guides it through covers for one.
On off, it is nicely defended.
Outside off, it is left alone. Another good over for the visitors.
On the pads, this is clipped nicely wide of fine leg and two is taken.
Fuller and on off, it comes back in late. Stokes mistimes it towards wide mid on for one. He is into the 90s now.
The batsman dances down the track and does well to block the ball.
FOUR! Deft again! A boundary is being scored every over now. Shorter and outside off, Stokes plays it late and down towards third man for a boundary.
Southee comes from around the wicket, he bowls it fuller and on middle, Stokes strokes it to mid on.
Outside off, this is left alone.
Good length and on off, Pope guides it to point.
One more delivery on a length and on off, this is defended.
Goes back to bowling length and on off, OP keeps it out.
FOUR! Pope is looking really good out there! Boult bowls this shorter and Pope picks it early, he rocks back and pulls it through square leg for another boundary. Runs flowing today.
Shorter and on the body, this is pulled through square leg and a single is taken.
Width on offer outside off, this is slapped through covers but there is protection in the deep so just the single.
Fuller and closer to the off pole, Stokes pushes it firmly but straight to mid off.
FOUR! Deft! Stokes moves into the 80s. This is a length delivery outside off, Stokes waits for it and then plays it pretty late through backward point for a boundary.
Drags his length back a little and lands it on off, Stokes keeps it out.
Fuller again and on off, no movement again. Stokes moves right across and strokes it to mid off.
Well no movement first up! It is outside off, left alone.
Tim Southee is on now! He should enjoy these conditions, it is nice and windy and he should get the ball to move.

BEATEN! That is Trent Boult for you. He bowls one on a length and in that channel of uncertainty. Pope looks to fiddle with it but is lucky as the ball goes past the outside edge and into the mitts of the keeper.
Good length and around off, Pope chooses to leave that alone.

FOUR! Beautiful shot from the bat of Pope. Boult is guilty of going short and Ollie is smart to read it as he pulls it off his back foot all along the ground. The ball races to the deep square leg fence in a flash.
Short of good length and on off, Pope defends it back to the bowler off his back foot.
Back of a length delivery on middle, Pope blocks it off his back foot to short mid-wicket.
Length delivery around off, Pope defends it off his front foot to the off side.
A single to end the over as Pope clips this through square leg for one.
Slips this one down the leg side, Pope looks to flick but misses.
Slightly fuller this time and outside off, Pope strokes it to the man at covers.
Good length and on off, Pope keeps it out nicely.
Outside off, Pope does not play at it.

On the fuller side and it tails back in from outside off, Stokes takes a few steps down the track and works it towards mid-wicket. The fielder there dives to his right and makes a half stop. Saves three for his side.
Boult bowls one on a length and around off, Pope blocks it off his back foot to the off side.
Length and outside off, Pope leaves it for Watling to grab it.
Fuller one on middle and off, Pope flicks it but finds mid on.
Short delivery on middle, Stokes pulls it through mid-wicket for a single.
On a good length and on middle and off, Stokes shuffles across and flicks it off his pad through mid-wicket for a couple.
Length and on off, Stokes blocks it solidly.
Outside off. This time Pope does not shuffle way too across and lets it be.

NOT OUT! It is going over! Well, did not see that coming, it seemed a good decision when we saw it first. Colin lands this on off and gets it to come back in. Pope takes a few steps down the track and also shuffles across to flick but misses. It hits the pad. An appeal and after a long thought, the umpire raises his finger. Stokes asks Pope to review and he does so. Replays roll in and they show that the on-field call has to be overturned. An excellent use of the review. Pope should be thanking Stokes here as he is the one who gave him the nod to do so.
Review time! Pope has been given out LBW but he reviews. He seems to have walked a long way across but also had taken a few steps ahead. Seems out though.
Attacks the stumps, Pope works it to mid-wicket.
Goes fuller again and on off, it tails back in. Stokes looks to drive but due to the movement it goes off the inner half through square leg for one. 250 up for England.
A couple! Very full and outside off, Stokes does not time it nicely but gets it past cover. The sweeper in the deep fields it and two is taken.
Colin starts this around off and then gets it to tail back in. Stokes pushes it to mid on.
On the shorter side and on off, Stokes stands tall and punches it wide of mid off and gets to the other end. A single to end the over. It just went for two but not a good one by Boult.
Finally makes the batter play, it is on off, Stokes prods forward and defends it solidly.
One more delivery which swings away but it is once again outside off, left alone.
Better! This starts around off and then moves away. Stokes makes another leave.
That has swung a long, long way but the line is outside off. Stokes leaves it alone. Watling collects it with a dive to his left in front of the first slip fielder.
Starts off with one on the pads, Pope looks to flick but the ball hits the pad and rolls down towards fine leg and a single is taken. It is signaled as a leg bye.
Trent Boult to bowl from the other end.
Another length and outside off, Stokes is happy to leave that one to see off the first over on Day 2.
Length and outside off, Colin brings the ball back in but not enough to  make Stokes play. Ben shoulders arms to it.
Length and around off, Ben leaves it for the keeper.

FOUR! First runs off the day. Ben starts from where he left the other day. De Grandhomme bowls one on a length and on off. Stokes just pushes it from within the crease back past the bowler. The fielder at mid on dives to his right but fails to field it. The ball races to the long on fence for a boundary.
Length and outside off, Stokes lets it be.
Length and outside off, Stokes defends it off the back foot. A good start with the ball from Colin de Grandhomme.

We are all set for the start of the first session of Day 2. Overnight batting pair of Ben Stokes and Ollie Pope are out in the middle. The New Zealand players are also taking their position in the field. Colin de Grandhomme to start the proceedings for the hosts. Here we go...

After all of that, it is the visitors who find their noses ahead at the moment. One more decent partnership will take them in a strong position. They have their best player in the past year or so Ben Stokes out there who is well-set and they will hope he along with the batters to come can take them close to 400. New Zealand on the other hand, will look to take early wickets with the second new ball which is relatively new. Another attritional day of cricket awaits.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the first Test between New Zealand and England. The visitors managed to amass 241 runs at a run rate of less than 3. Now when I write that, you would probably feel it was a boring day of Test cricket. That though was not the case, it wasn't an exciting day but it was an excellent battle between bat and ball where the bowlers had to work hard to create chances and the batters too weren't given away easy opportunities to score.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Now then, one more good partnership and England will have a good first innings score. However, if New Zealand manage to take a few wickets early on Day 2, they would be right back into this. An action-packed day awaits. Do join us at 1100 local (2200 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

The New Zealand bowling was very disciplined, they did not begin that well but once they got into their rhythm, they did not let runs leak quickly. They did manage to take timely wickets with Colin de Grandhomme being the pick for them. Boult however was a touch disappointing as he did not look at his best. Also, had they hung onto Stokes' catch right at the end, they would have slept a lot better.

Right from the start things went as the visitors wanted it to. To begin with, they won the toss and elected to bat and then they managed to put up decent stands. The openers set the tone with Burns scoring a half ton. However, Rory and Root fell in quick succession but Stokes and Denly put up an 83-run stand which meant England remained on top. Both scored half tons but the latter failed to make most of the start he got. Stokes however, is still battling it out, he is joined by Pope who would be eager to prove his mettle.

End of a hard-fought day of Test cricket! Both the sides had to toil hard. The English, for every run they had to score and the Kiwis as picking wickets was just not easy. In the end however, one can say, it is the English side who is just ahead at the moment.
Last ball of the day and it is wide outside off, left alone by Pope. England end Day 1 on 241/4.
FOUR! Short delivery on middle and leg, Pope rocks back and pulls this one superbly to the mid-wicket fence. No nerves for Ollie before the end of the day's play.
Another one way outside off, Pope does not have to fiddle with it.
Way wide outside off, Pope does not bother to play at that.
Great movement for Boult here. He bowls it on a length around off, it pitches and moves away. Ollie confidently shoulders arms.
Length ball wide outside off, left alone by Ollie.
On the pads of Stokes, he looks to flick but misses. He is hit on the pads.
Third time in a row, delivered outside off and Stokes shoulders arms to it.
Another one outside off, left alone by Stokes.
Outside off, left alone by Ben.
Back of a length on middle, pulled away towards square leg for a single.

DROPPED AND FOUR! Second chance that has been missed in this match and Taylor the culprit in both of them. Another back of a length ball on off, Stokes again looks to go for the same shot. However, this time, Stokes thick edges it which goes straight to Ross Taylor at first slip. He was late to react and thus, the ball goes through his hands and into the third man fence. Again it looked like Taylor was expecting Latham to come for the catch from second slip but the ball was going straight to him. Could prove very costly for the Kiwis this.
FOUR! Three in three! Stokes looking elegant as ever! Back of a length ball on off, Stokes gets on his toes and drives this one through the cover region for a boundary!
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries! This time on the pads, Stokes flicks this one behind square where he beats the fielder in the deep as the ball races to the fence.
FOUR! Superb timing! Full on off, Stokes prods forward and just punches it through mid off for a boundary.
Boult bowls a yorker wide outside off, Stokes looks to dig it out but misses.
Stokes pushes this one towards covers and takes a single.
Down the leg side, Stokes looks to flick this one but misses.
Outside off, Ben leaves it alone.

50 for Ben Stokes! He has looked calm and composed out in the middle and has attacked the bowlers when required as well. This one is on the pads of Stokes, he flicks this one towards the mid-wicket region and gets a couple.
Another ball which is wide outside off, Stokes does not bother to play at it.
Outside off, Stokes leaves it alone.
Length ball on middle and off, defended off the back foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Caught in two minds but Pope survives. Length ball on off, Pope first looks to defend but eventually opts to leave the ball. However, he is too late in taking his bat away from the line of the ball. The ball takes the toe end of the bat and goes towards the point region.
FOUR! Free runs for the batsman. Drifting down leg, Pope just glances this one fine down the leg side and gets a boundary.
This time Ollie defends this one off the back foot.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Pope.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Fuller on off, pushed towards cover for a single. Pope is off the mark.
Ollie Pope is the new man.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! The stand which was worrying the Kiwis has been cut short. Denly, like numerous times in his career, fails to make most of the start he got. A good delivery this by Southee. He bowls a good length ball just outside off, the ball angles in and straightens after pitching. Denly again gets an outside edge on this one as he tries to defend but this time it carries to the right of Watling. He dives and takes it with one hand in front of the first slip fielder. The second new ball does the trick for the Kiwis. Still time to go before Stumps, can they take one more?
FOUR! 200 up for England and in grand fashion! Full ball outside off, Denly creams this one through the cover region.
Length ball on off, Denly shoulders arms to let that one through.

EDGED BUT JUST SHORT! Southee bowls a jaffa right after coming into the attack. He bowls it fullish on the off pole and gets it to move away. Denly looks to defend with soft hands. The ball goes off the outside edge towards the man at second slip but falls just short.
Tim Southee comes back from the other end. 16-5-30-0, his figures so far.
Full ball on off, Denly pushes this towards cover and takes a single. Retains strike.
Fuller ball on off, Denly looks to push this one towards the off side but the ball goes off the inside half towards mid-wicket.
Length ball on off, Denly shoulders arms.
Full ball on middle this time, Denly pushes it straight back to the bowler.
Full ball on off, pushed towards the mid off region.
Good length ball on middle, Denly looks to defend but the ball goes off the inside edge towards square leg.
Trent Boult comes back to operate with the second new ball.
Second new ball available now and Kane Williamson has taken it straightaway.
On the pads, worked towards mid-wicket.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Stokes works it fine down the leg side and takes a couple.
Floated on middle again, Denly pushes it with soft hands towards mid on for one.
Down the leg side, Denly goes after it but misses.
Floated on middle and off, pushed back towards the bowler.
The batsman opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man.

Everything happening out in the middle! Wagner bowls a good length ball around leg, Stokes is late in getting his bat down. The ball hits the pad and the New Zealand players appeal but the umpire is unmoved. Replays roll in and show that it goes off the inside edge onto the pads. The ball rolls towards the off side and Denly sets off for the single. The fielder, Williamson, rushes in, picks up the ball and has a shy at the striker's end but misses. The ball goes towards square leg and the batters take a single.
On off, Denly pushes this one towards the man at mid off.
Back of a length ball on middle, pulled away by Stokes towards mid-wicket for one.
Another full ball on off, Denly works this one towards point for one.
Fullish on off, pushed towards the man at mid off.
Full and outside off, Stokes goes for the reverse sweep and gets it towards third man. The batsmen take a couple.
Denly cuts this short one through point for a single.
Tossed up ball on off, Stokes drives it through mid off for a run.
Flighted ball on off, Denly drives it to long off for a run.
Denly looks to defend this full ball but gets it off the inside edge. The ball just falls short of the short leg fielder.
Tossed up ball on off, Denly defends it off the front foot to the off side.
Length and outside off, Stokes drives it to covers.
Wagner bowls a knuckle ball and bowls it extremely full Stokes squeezes it to the off side.
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries off the bat of Stokes. Wagner once again goes short and on middle, Stokes pulls it just wide off mid on and into the mid-wicket fence for a boundary.
UPPISH AND FOUR! Wagner bowls short and wide outside off, Stokes cuts it over the point fielder and gets a boundary.
Length and around off, Stokes drives it handsomely to covers.
Length and outside off, Stokes shoulders arms to it.
Denly blocks this tossed up ball off the back foot solidly.
Three in a row. Denly once again defends this flighted one to the off side.
Fuller one outside off, Denly once again finds short cover to perfection.
Flatter one outside off, Denly drives it to short cover.
Tossed up on middle, Stokes works it to mid-wicket for a single.
Short and wide outside off, Stokes cuts it off the back foot through covers for a couple.
Good length ball on off, Stokes strokes it towards cover and takes a single to retain strike.
Outside off, cut towards point.
FOUR! Beauty! Pure class! Full ball on off, Stokes just takes a step ahead and punches this ball down the ground through mid on for a boundary.
On off, pushed towards the man extra cover.
Fuller one this time, again pushed towards mid off.
Length ball on off, pushed towards mid off.

SIX! What a magnificent hit! Santner bowls another full ball and Denly lofts it straight over the bowler's head and into the sightscreen for a maximum. First one off this Test from Joe's bat. Another 50-run stand also comes up between Joe Denly and Ben Stokes. Will this pair take England off unaffected at the close of play?
Santner defends this flatter one off the full face off the bat.
FOUR! Beautifully lofted. Santner bowls one full on middle, Denly makes room and lofts it over the covers. The ball races to the extra cover fence for a boundary.
Denly blocks this tossed up ball to the off side.
Tossed up on around middle, Denly works it to mid-wicket.
Flighted on off, Stokes drives it to long on for a run.

Drinks Break! A mixed session so far. England have lost their skipper for a low score yet again but Stokes and Denly have stood strong. The Kiwis have been patient with their bowling and with the day coming to its latter stages, they would now be looking to at least increase the over rate.
Another length ball outside off, Denly defends it solidly.
Length and around off, Denly defends it to the off side.
Good length and outside off, Denly drives it to mid off.
Good length and outside off, Denly is happy to let that go.
Length and on middle, Swinging in towards the pads. Denly flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Back of a length around off, Stokes pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Outside off, Denly guides this one down to third man for a couple.

Denly survives! Chance of a run out as soon as Santner comes into the attack. Floated on middle, Denly looks to work this one towards the leg side. He does so but straight to Latham at short leg who grabs the ball at the first attempt. Denly is couple of yards out of his crease but Latham hesitates to throw it at the striker's end. The most that it would have cost his team would have been a couple of overthrow runs. The Kiwis should be taking these kind of chances.
The wait is finally over, on comes Mitchell Santner after 71 overs. It will be interesting to see if he gets some sort of purchase.
Good Length and on off, Stokes blocks it solidy.
FOUR! Full and outside off, Stokes this time doesn't miss out as Wagner gives him lots of width. Ben just drives it superbly through covers and fetches himself a boundary.
Length and on off, Stokes gets it off the inside edge to mid-wicket.
Length and outside off, Big Ben leaves it for the keeper.
Fuller length and outside off, Stokes drives it straight to the man at mid off.
Length and  outside off, Stokes just leaves it alone.
Fullish on middle and off, pushed back towards the bowler.
On the pads, Stokes works this one towards mid-wicket for one.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Stokes.
Fuller this time, Ben pushes this one towards the off side.
Another good length ball, angling into the batter. Stokes blocks it out.
Good length ball on the pads, worked towards mid-wicket.
Denly attempts to put bat on ball but fails.
Good length delivery around off, Denly drives it to mid off.
Length and outside off, In that channel of certainty as Denly watches the ball closely as it goes past the off pole.

FOUR! What a way to get to your 5th Test fifty! It's England's reliable batsman, Joe Denly. A very patient knock by him. He has literally dug it out there and now he would not want to throw it away. He has got in and he should be eyeing a big one. He gets a gift to get to that milestone, full and wide outside off, it is hit through covers for a boundary.
Full and outside off, Denly drives it straight to mid off.
Fuller length and on pads,  stokes flicks it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Neil Wagner is back on! His figures so far read 17-4-49-1.
Good length and outside off, Stokes drives it through covers for a single. New Zealand are giving nothing away here.

Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Fullish ball on off, pushed to the man at mid off.

Nice fielding by Santner, Backing up his fellow bowler! Full ball wide outside off, Stokes creams his drive towards the cover region. However, Santner there dives to his right and makes a very good stop. No runs taken.
On the pads, Stokes flicks this one towards square leg for a couple.
Length ball outside off, Stokes shoulders arms.
Fuller ball on off, pushed towards extra cover.
A little too straight, this is worked behind square on the leg side for two.
Shorter and on off, Denly stands tall and keeps it out.

Another back of a length delivery on off, JD stays back and defends it onto the ground.
On the stumps this time, Denly gets right behind the line and keeps it out.

Taylor there misses it and the ball goes between his legs towards the third man fence. Watling gives it the chase, dives and pulls it in just before the ball reaches the ropes. The batters are able to take two.
Length ball just outside off, defended off the back foot by Stokes.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Stokes.
Shortish on middle, Stokes leaves it alone.

Full ball on off, Stokes pushes this one towards the man at mid off.
Outside off, left alone.

Fuller on off, pushes this one wide of mid off.

BEAUTY! This is angled into the batter, it pitches and then shapes away. Denly pokes at it and gets beaten.

Once again, not very full but on a length and around off, it is kept out.

Excellent fielding! Williamson is the man, the skipper leading from the front here. Fuller and on off, Denly strokes it towards extra cover. Williamson at mid off dives and stops it. A single only.

Welcome back for the last session of the day. Kane Williamson leads his troops out  followed by the English pair of Joe Denly and Ben Stokes. Will New Zealand chip in with wickets or will England edge ahead? Action unfolds for one last time on Day 1 as Neil Wagner starts the session with the ball.
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

New Zealand were better with the ball in this session. They toiled hard and managed to break the Burns/Denly partnership. Colin de Grandhomme picked up another wicket with Neil Wagner rightfully getting the wicket as he looked the most lethal in this session. The hosts would look to continue this in the final session. The question is will they be able to? Join us after the break to find out.

A good session for the Kiwis. They struggled at the start with Burns and Denly fighting it out but the wicket of Burns after his fifty got the hosts going. Root then joined Denly and though the English skipper took his time to get off the mark he did not wait long after that. In fact his 30 odd minute stay yielded just 2 runs. The visitors would look to re-gather themselves and refocus again.

Replay rolls in and shows Stokes is good in his back up as he was back in his crease.

OUT! Caught! Simple catching practice for Tim Southee at second slip. Root took his time to set in but cannot make it count as he departs the very next ball after getting off the mark. Good length ball outside off, Root goes poking after it. It takes a thick outside edge and goes to the right of Tim Southee at second slip. He shows good reflexes and takes a sharp catch. Not a heroic welcome for the English skipper back at no.4. All-rounder Ben Stokes replaces his skipper out in the middle.
A huge cheer from the crowd. Root is finally off the mark on the 21st ball. Full on middle and leg, Root flicks it through square leg. Jeet Raval there misfields allowing Root to get a couple.

Length delivery on off, Denly defends it out.
Boult comes round the wicket now and the change of angle almost immediately works for him. Denly looks to defend this one off the back foot but it goes off the inside edge onto the pads.

Denly pushes this one towards cover-point for a single.

On off, pushed towards the cover region.
Full ball outside off, swinging away. Denly drives it towards the cover region where Santner dives and saves runs.
Another full delivery outside off, Root guides it to point and he wants the single but it is not there.

Good length ball on off, Root defends it to cover.

On off, defends it out.
Good length ball on middle, Denly defends it out.
Fullish delivery on off, Joe drives it to mid off.
On a length on off, Denly defends it to cover for nothing.

Another one outside off, this time pushed towards point.

Fullish on middle, Denly works this one wide of mid on for a quick single.

England skipper, Joe Root walks out at number 4.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Burns does not hang around after getting to his fifty. Once again it is Colin de Grandhomme who has given his skipper the much-needed breakthrough. Colin de Grandhomme bowls it slightly fuller outside off, Burns has a poke at it and gets an outside edge which goes straight into the the mitts of Watling. He makes no mistake and New Zealand finally find a way to get rid of this stand.
Again on the pads, Burns flicks this one towards square leg and takes a single. Retains strike for the next over.
Way outside off, left alone by Burns.

FOUR! 50 for Burns! Lovely shot by Rory! Too straight by Boult, Burns shuffles and flicks this one nonchalantly towards mid-wicket for a boundary. What a way to get to your 5th Test half ton and he will be looking to convert this start into a ton now.
On the pads of Burns, he flicks this one behind square leg and takes a quick couple.
Fullish on off, pushed towards the man at mid on.
On the pads, tucked towards mid-wicket.
BEATEN! Excellent bowling from de Grandhomme! Bowls it on a length outside off, Rory looks to defend it but it whizzes past the bat and into the mitts of the keeper.
Very full delivery outside off swinging in a little, Burns attempts to drive but misses the ball completely.

Colin de Grandhomme comes back into the attack. 9-2-19-1 are his figures so far.
On the pads, worked towards the man at mid-wicket.

NOT OUT! Height is an issue but only by just. Umpire's call it is! Close call that and the Kiwis can count themselves a touch unfortunate but they don't lose a review so that can be counted as a consolation. Boult bowls a good length ball just outside off, gets it to swing back into the batter. Burns looks to defend but plays outside the line of the delivery. He misses to get hit on the thigh pad of his back leg. A huge appeal from the New Zealand players follows but the umpire is unmoved. Williamson has a chat with his teammates and goes for the review. The replays roll in, Ultra Edge shows no bat involved. Hawk Eye comes in, and shows to be clipping the off pole. A jaffa but no reward for Boult!
Boult bowls a good length ball just outside off, defended out by Burns.
Review time! New Zealand have taken the review for an LBW against Rory Burns. Height seems to be an issue. Let's see what the replays have to say.

Wagner has bowled really well but does not have a wicket to show for it. Kiwi skipper, Kane Williamson needs his bowlers to find a way to get rid of this partnership.

Edged but falls short. Good length ball on off, Denly looks to defend it with soft hands. He misreads the swing and ends up getting a thick edge towards first slip. Luckily he does not go hard at it and hence the ball does not carry to Ross Taylor at first slip.

Burns looks to defend but the ball takes a thick outside edge and goes right between first and second slip. Taylor at first and Latham at second think the other one is going to go after it. Southee should have had a wicket here and Wagner's aggression had played its part but lack of communication at slips has made it unsuccessful.

Bouncer again from Wagner. Rory ducks under it.
Fuller outside off, asking Burns to drive. Rory does go after it but misses.
Wagner continues to steam in. Back of a length ball on off, Burns keeps his eyes on the ball and tucks it to square leg.

The physio is out now. Burns is going through the mandatory concussion test and getting his helmet changed. He looks fine but nothing can be taken lightly when it comes to a head injury as we have seen federations taking it more seriously, not just in cricket but in all sports.
FOUR LEG BYES! Nasty! Brilliant short ball from Wagner! Burns looks to get down but he is a bit late. The ball glances his helmet and lobs over the slips to the fence. That will wind Burns a bit.
Good length ball on the pads, Denly tucks it to the on side and gets to the other end.
On middle and off, Burns pushes this one back towards Southee. Tim tries to gather the ball and throw it back but the ball goes through his legs towards mid on.
Another full ball, this time on off, pushed towards cover by Burns.
Full ball on middle, pushed towards the man at mid on.
Length ball on off, pushed to the man at point.
Length ball wide outside off, Burns looks to have a powerful slash at it but misses.
Starts with a good length ball on off, pushed towards the man at cover.

FOUR! Nailed! Wagner goes short again, Denly is ready for it. He rocks back and pulls it to the right of the fielder at deep square leg for another boundary. Excellent response after getting beaten all ends up on the last delivery.

OHHH! That has missed the off pole by a whisker. Not sure what Joe Denly was beaten by! Was it the late movement or was he just expecting a short ball and maybe got his bat down late? Both actually. Wagner goes fuller and this one starts outside off. It comes back in late. Denly initially looks to leave but then tries to get his bat down in time. However, he fails to do so. It almost kisses the off pole.
Wagner goes back to bowling fuller, it is on off, Denly plays it late, it goes towards gully where de Grandhomme dives and stops it.
FOUR! Hammered! This time the pull shot is nailed! Denly has decided to take on the short balls here. He goes back and pulls it hard through mid-wicket. No chance for the fielder in the deep.
Underedge! Maybe that wasn't a very good shot. It is shorter and around off, angling away. Denly looks to drag it but gets an underedge towards mid-wicket.
Angles this one away after landing it on a length around off, Denly lets it be.
Denly flicks this one off his pads towards mid-wicket for a single.
On middle and off, punched back towards the bowler. Southee picks the ball up and fakes a throw at the striker's end. Signs of aggression!
EDGED BUT SAFE! Good length ball on off, it moves away a bit. Denly looks to have a poke at it but the ball goes off the edge towards gully but on the bounce.
Length ball on off, Burns steers this one towards point for one.
This time way wide outside off, Burns looks to have a slash at it but misses.
Length ball on middle and off, defended out by Burns.
Another bouncer, Denly again ducks under it. An interesting battle going on between Wagner and Denly. It is the Englishman who has won it in this over.
Bouncer on middle and leg, ducked under by Denly now.

FOUR! Pulled away again! Brilliant reply from Denly after almost getting caught on the previous ball. Wagner goes short around the body, Joe expected it. He transfers his weight onto his back foot and pulls it with sheer power through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Edged but just short! Good length ball on off, it swings away at the end. Denly looks to defend but ends up edging it towards point. Luckily for Denly the ball falls short of the man there.
Short of a length ball on middle, Denly looks to have a poke at it but is beaten.
FOUR! Right above the man at short leg! Back of a length delivery on middle, Denly rocks back and pulls this one towards square leg for a boundary.
Too wide outside off, Burns initially thought about playing at it but then shoulders arms.
Shortish on middle, Denly pulls this one towards backward square leg for one.
Another fuller ball on off, Denly looks to push it towards the off side but the ball goes off the inside half towards the man at mid on.
Fuller ball on off, pushed to the man at extra cover.
Another one on off, left alone by Denly this time.
Length ball on off, pushed towards the man at mid off.
Similar ball down the leg side again, this time Burns goes after it but misses.
Back of a length down the leg side, Burns leaves it alone.
Another length ball on off, pushed back towards the bowler by Burns.
Length ball on middle and off, defended by the batter.
Good fielding in the deep by Santner. On off by Wagner, Denly drives this one towards the point region. Santner gives this one the chase, dives and just about keeps it in play. 3 runs taken.
On the pads of Denly, he flicks this one towards square leg for a couple.
Neil Wagner to bowl from the other end to start the session.
Length ball just outside off, left alone. Good over to start off post Lunch for Southee.
Beauty! Jaffa to beat Burns! Fullish ball outside off, Burns looks to drive at this one but the ball just moves away ands beats the outside edge of Burns' blade.
3rd time in a row, full delivery outside off, it is pushed towards the cover fielder who has been a busy man as he fields the ball again.
Full outside off, pushed towards the man at cover again.
Full length ball again outside off, Burns pushes this powerfully towards cover but the fielder there dives to his right and holds onto the ball.
Southee starts with a full length ball wide outside off, Burns pushes it to the man at mid off.

Welcome back for the second session. The Kiwi players are out on the field, the English batting pair of Rory Burns and Joe Denly walks out to resume their innings. Tim Southee to start the afternoon session with the ball.
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

New Zealand have bowled to a plan and one has to say they have patiently stuck to it. Colin de Grandhomme was the only bowler to pick up a wicket but the rest were good with the cherry in hand. Will they continue to stick to their plan or will England's patience see them change their plans? Join us for the second session to find out.

A proper fighting session of Test cricket. England openers, Sibley and Burns fought out the hard times and got the visitors off to a good start but the debutant was unable to convert that start and was dismissed by Colin de Grandhomme. Denly then joined Rory Burns out in the middle and the duo ensured that England went into Lunch with just the loss of one wicket.
A good ball to end the session! Good length and on off, this one takes off after pitching. Denly plays it well by taking one hand off the handle. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 1!
A little too straight this time, it is worked towards mid-wicket.
Good length and on middle, Denly stays back and keeps it out nicely.
Well bowled and well played! Goes full and gets it to tail back in from middle. Denly gets his bat down and pushes it to mid off.
Another short one on the body, this is worked down to fine leg for one.
A short one from around the wicket, angling away from the batter. Burns drops his hands and lets it go to the keeper.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Good length ball on off, pushed towards mid on.
FOUR! Beautifully driven! Full and wide outside off, Denly prods forwards and just caresses this through the cover region for a boundary.
On the pads, worked towards the leg side.
Length ball on off, pushed towards mid on off the back foot.
Way outside off, left alone by Denly.

A stifled appeal for a catch has been turned down by the umpire. Wagner bowls a wonderful bouncer, angling away from the batter. Burns looks to sway away from it and drop his arms. He does so just in time as replays show that the ball has hit Burns' shoulder on its way to the fielder at second slip. However, the replay of Wagner's bowling run-up later comes in and shows that he had overstepped while bowling the delivery. The bowler is lucky to get away with that.
Wagner comes around the wicket this time, pitches it outside leg and makes it to angle away from the batter. Burns works it towards the square leg region.
Down the leg side, Burns looks to flick but misses.
Full ball on off, pushed towards point.
Bouncer down the leg side, Burns ducks under it.
Length ball on off, defended out by Burns.
Outside off, left alone.
Fuller on middle, pushed towards mid on.
This time Colin bowls it closer to the off pole, but Denly knows exactly where it is and shoulders arms.
Fullish on off, pushed towards cover again.
On the fifth stump line, Denly shoulders arms.
Good length ball on off, pushed towards cover.
Another dot! On the shorter side and on the body, this is worked to the man at mid-wicket.
Another back of a length and on off, Burns keeps it out again.
Well played! Another shorter one on middle, Rory gets on top of the bounce and keeps it out.
Goes back to bowling it short and on the body, Rory evades it.
Well bowled! Very well bowled actually. Wagner kept bowling short, he throws this one full and outside off, Burns goes after it but his feet are rooted to the crease, Burns' bat is beaten.
A sharp bumper on middle, it is ducked under.
Another one on the stumps, this is defended.
On middle, it is kept out.
Uppish but short! Fuller and on off, Denly looks to hit it through mid on but is a touch early in the shot. It goes on the bounce to mid on.
That is a brave, brave leave! This lands around off and then moves away a touch. Denly sees the movement and lets it be. It goes really close past the off pole.
Width on offer outside off, Burns slaps it through point for three.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Outside off, on a good length, left alone.
Another one short of a length, Denly this time tucks it towards the leg side.
Short of a length ball on the body, Denly defends it onto the pitch.
Good length ball, close to the off pole but Denly knows exactly where it is and confidently shoulders arms.
Bouncer on middle and off, Denly ducks under it.
Length ball on middle and leg, pushed towards square leg for one.
One more ball outside off, Denly does not fiddle with it.
Another outswinger but outside off, it is left alone.
Joe Denly is the next man in.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! There is the breakthrough New Zealand so desperately needed. They looked off color till now but they will hope this wicket gets their tails up. Colin de Grandhomme is the one to break the solid-looking opening stand. Sibley, the debutant falls after getting off to a start. The ploy to keep it outside off has worked. He was constantly playing those deliveries away from his body or ahead of his body. Here too, Colin bowls it fuller and around off, it shapes away late. Sibley pushes at it with hard hands and ahead of his body. It goes off the outside edge, low and to Taylor's right at first slip. He dives and takes a good catch.

A loud, loud shout for both, caught behind and LBW but nothing. This is around off and then moves away. Sibley looks to defend but the ball hits the top of the pad and goes towards the keeper who takes it and appeals but not given. The impact was outside off.
One more ball on a length and on middle, this is worked towards mid-wicket.
A length delivery and on off, Sibley keeps it out.
Bouncer down the leg side, Burns does not bother to play at it. The Kiwi bowlers need to bowl better and make the batters play.
This time down the leg side, Burns looks to flick but misses.
Bouncer on middle again, Burns shuffles across but eventually ducks under it.
Fullish outside off, Burns leaves it alone.
Another bouncer on middle, Burns again ducks under it.
Good ball to start off the over. Bouncer on middle and off, Burns ducks under it.
Full ball on off, pushed back towards Colin by Sibley.
Full ball on off, Sibley gets low and awkwardly jams this one out towards the mid-wicket region.
Sibley prods forward and flicks this one towards the mid-wicket fielder.
Another ball on middle and off, again worked towards mid-wicket. The batsmen get a single.
Good length ball on off, worked towards mid-wicket.
Length ball on off, tucked towards square leg for a single.
A yorker but outside off, Burns jams it out to point.
Good length and on off, this is defended onto the ground.

Three taken! Also, fifty is up for England. Excellent opening stand for them after electing to bat. This is on the pads, it is worked through mid-wicket. Latham from mid-wicket runs after it and just before it crosses the ropes, pushes it back in.
Shorter and just outside off, Sibley thinks of playing at it but then bails out.
On the fuller side again, this is driven to the man at mid off.
Fuller and on off, Sibley pushes it back to the bowler.
Gets this one to come back in from outside off, Burns keeps it out nicely.
Looks to bring it back in from way outside off but it goes straight on. Burns shoulders arms to this one.
Outside off, it is not played at.
Starts this outside off and then gets it to tail back in. It is kept out.
FOUR! Nice and fine! Runs coming quickly! This is down the leg side, Burns tickles it fine and the ball races to the fine leg fence. The Kiwis haven't got it right till now.
Fuller and on middle, it is tailing back in. Burns strokes it to mid on.
FOUR! Easy pickings for Sibley! Wagner bowls it on the pads, Sibley works it through square leg and the ball races away to the fence.
Gets it right this time! On off and on a length. Sibley keeps it out.
So two balls down the leg side to start with, the next two outside off which is left alone by Sibley.
Outside off this time but it is left alone.
One more delivery down the leg side, Sibley initially looks to flick but then bails out.
FOUR! A poor delivery to begin with. Down the leg side, Sibley flicks it to the fine leg fence. Easy runs for Sibley, he loves it there.
Neil Wagner is on!
Goes back to over the wicket and lands it on the pads, it is worked towards mid-wicket.
Colin comes from around the wicket and bowls it fuller on off, it is worked with the angle to mid-wicket.
On the pads, this is worked down to fine leg and a single is taken.
One more delivery on a length and around off, Sibley pushes it to mid on.
Outside off, this is not played at.
This is angled into the pads, it is worked behind square on the leg side for one.
On off, it is kept out.

Change of angle almost does the trick. Boult runs in from around the wicket and bowls this outside off. Sibley looks to play at it due to the angle but gets beaten. It was a delivery he could have left but ended up playing at it due to the round the wicket angle.
Outside off again, this is not played at.
Well bowled! This lands on off and then moves away. Sibley defends the original trajectory and gets beaten.
This one lands on off, Sibley defends it out.

Very good shot! Fuller and shaping away from off. Burns leans into it nicely and pushes it through covers. The fielder from point hares after it, dives and pushes it back in. The other fielder from mid off does the mopping up job. Three taken.

DRINKS! England's first hour! Their openers have looked nice and solid and are amidst a good-looking stand. The visitors would want the same to continue. New Zealand on the other hand, have been a little wayward, they haven't hit the right lines and have hence been unable to trouble the English openers. It has not gone all that well for them but they would hope it would change after the break.
Good length ball outside off, Sibley lets it carry to the keeper.
Colin continues to test his patience and bowls it outside off again.  Dom leaves it alone.
Well wide outside off, Sibley at this point of time is ready to wait as he leaves it alone.
Good length ball around off, Sibley gets behind the line of the ball and taps it back to CdG.
Full on middle, Burns flicks it to deep square leg for one.
Full on off, Burns defends it to mid off.
Very full on middle and leg, Burns flicks it through mid-wicket and gets a single to get through the over.
On the fuller side and on off, Burns keeps it out towards mid off.
A little too straight, this is worked around the corner and a single is taken.
Just outside off, Sibley covers his off pole and lets it go to the keeper.
Good running! This is on off, Burns pushes it to the left of point and gets to the other end.
Fuller and on off, this is driven back to the bowler.
Fuller on off, Burns flicks it through square leg. Boult manages to save it before the ropes, saves a run for his side.
Back of a length, Rory defends it off the back foot.
Outside off, Burns leaves it alone.
Edged but safe. Fuller on off and middle, Burns looks to defend on the on side but gets a leading edge towards point. Luckily it does not carry.
Goes outside off now, Burns leaves it alone.
De Grandhomme starts with a good length ball on off, Burns keeps it out.
Bowling change. First one of the day. Colin de Grandhomme is into the attack.
Oh that was close! Full outside off, Sibley decides to have a poke at it but is fortunate to not edge it.
Boult goes a bit short this time outside off, Dominic sways away from it.
Outside off, Sibley leaves it alone.
Full and coming in, Sibley keeps his eyes on the ball and flicks it to short mid-wicket.
Back of a length on off, Sibley defends it to the on side this time.
Good length ball on off, Sibley defends it with a straight bat.
Full and going away outside off, Burns once again is not tempted to drive that.
Southee corrects his line and bowls it fuller outside off. He wants Burns to drive but Rory is happy to let it go.

FOUR! A rare loose delivery and Burns is ready to pounce on it in a flash. Back of a length ball outside off, Burns gets on his back foot and punches it through point right off the meat for a boundary.
A short one on the body, Burns ducks under it.
Outside off, left alone.
On off, this is pushed to the man at mid off.
This is closer to the off pole, Sibley keeps it out easily.
Angles this across the batter but ends up bowling it too wide outside off, not played at.
Back of a length and on off, Burns plays it late through backward point and takes one. A run after 15 balls off Boult's bowling.
Angles this one into the batter, Burns is solid in defense.
A sharp bouncer but it is spotted early by Burns. He evades it.
Off the outer half! Full and on middle, it moves away late. Burns looks to drive it with a straight bat but it goes off the outer half towards point.

FOUR! Once again a brilliant flick shot. This is fuller and on middle from Southee. Sibley shuffles across and then flicks it against the movement and through mid-wicket for one more boundary. He is on 8 and both the boundaries he scored have been hit in that area.
Slips this one down the leg side, Sibley looks to flick but misses.
Fuller and on middle, Sibley strokes it towards mid on who moves to his right and stops it nicely.
A good bumper but once again it is down the leg side, Sibley ducks under it with ease.
A harmless delivery, outside off, it is not played at.
Fuller and on middle, Sibley pushes it to mid on.
BEATEN! Once again the last ball is a beauty! This is a length delivery on off, it moves away late. Burns defends inside the line and gets beaten.
Fuller and on middle, Burns strokes it nicely but Boult gets down and stops it.
Better! This is what he needs to do more, make the batter play. Attacks the stumps this time, Burns keeps it out nicely.
One more delivery outside off, not played at. Boult has not made the batter play enough. He has been a little too wide.
Slightly fuller but outside off, it is left alone.
Fuller and on off, Burns strokes it to mid off.
A crisp drive to end but for no runs! A maiden by Southee. Fuller and on off, Sibley strokes it to mid off.
Goes fuller this time and bowls it on the stumps. Sibley lunges and keeps it out.
Outside off, Sibley need not play at those.
Good length again and on off, DS goes back and keeps it out.
Fuller and outside off, Sibley lets it be.
Back of a length and on off, Sibley keeps it out.

A stifled appeal but nothing! Finally Boult gets one right and he beats the outside edge. This is a length delivery, it is angled into the off pole but then leaves the batter. Burns looks to defend but is beaten. An appeal but not a confident one. Not given. Well, well, well, Hot Spot rolls in later on and it shows the tiniest of marks as it goes past the bat. It is very, very slight to say the least. Can't blame anyone for that as it looked to be missing the bat to the naked eye and one would need to have scanning vision to detect that.
Attacks the stumps and Burns pushes it to mid on.
One more shorter in length delivery on middle, Burns ducks under it.
On the fuller side and on off, Burns strokes it towards extra cover.
On a length and around off, Burns defends it on the leg side.
On the fuller side and outside off, Burns does not fiddle with it.
On the fuller side but the line is outside off, tempting the batsman to go after it. Sibley does not fiddle with it. Maiden from Southee! First one of the game!
Goes short this time but down the leg side, it is ducked under.
This starts on middle and then moves away. Sibley gets right behind the line and is solid in defense.
Attacks the off pole this time, Sibley shows the full face of the bat and hits it to mid on.
Goes wide of the crease and bowls this one outside off, Sibley does not play at it.
Good length and outside off, it is left alone.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for Burns. England are off to a brisk start here. Boult looks to bowl the magic delivery, he tries to swing it from the leg pole to the off. No movement and it is clipped past square leg and it races away to the fence.

FOUR! Just a mere push for Burns' first boundary! Lovely shot. Fuller and on middle, Burns shows the full face of the bat and hits it down towards the long on fence. Mid on gives it a chase but he has no chance despite a dive.
Well bowled! This is angled into the middle pole, no swing this time. Burns pushes it to short mid-wicket.
And again, too wide outside off, Burns will not be going after those so early in his innings.
One more delivery wide outside off, Burns shoulders arms to this one. Boult is getting the ball to move nicely, the line is not that great though.
Outside off and it moves away further. Left alone.
Fuller outside off, Dominic lunges forward and leaves it alone.
Southee pulls his length back on this occasion, Sibley keeps his eyes on the ball and blocks it.
Another ball outside off, Sibley shoulders arms to it.
Good length ball outside off, it goes away from the batter. Sibley does not go chasing after it and leaves it alone.

Direct Hit and Sibley could have been in trouble. Fuller on off and middle, Burns tucks it towards short mid-wicket and calls for a quick single. Sibley responds to his partner and keeps his head down and steams to the other end. Jeet Raval gets to the ball quickly and has a shy at the keeper's end but misses. Dominic puts in a dive. Replays show the dive might have saved Sibley. You do not want to get run out in Tests especially on your debut.
Little shape in for Southee first up. Fuller ball angling in from middle and off, Burns defends it with a straight bat.
Tim Southee to partner Trent Boult with the new ball.

FOUR! That is some way to score your first Test runs! A lovely clip off the pads. This is fuller and tailing back in from middle. Sibley was ready for it, he does not plant his front foot way too across and just flicks it through mid-wicket. It races away.
England are underway! This one goes off the inside edge. Fuller and on off, it goes on with the angle. Burns plays outside the line this time, it goes off the inner half towards fine leg for one.

Edged and short! Played that with soft hands! Another length delivery around middle, it moves away. Burns plays it with soft hands but does so inside the line. It goes off the outside edge but well short of third slip.
Swing again! On a length and around off, shapes away again. Burns initially looks to play but then pulls his bat back.
Lands this one on a length and around off, some shape away from the batter. Burns is solid in defense.

An aggressive start by Boult. He starts off with a bumper so the ball does not get any chance of doing its bit. Burns spots it and ducks under it. Maybe a bouncer because we saw Burns struggling against that delivery against Australia a few months back. He played that one well though.

We are all set for the action to begin! The Kiwi players make their way out to the middle. They are followed by a new English opening pair of Rory Burns and Dominic Sibley. The left-hander will be on strike and he will be facing Trent Boult. Will he get some swing early on? We will find out as he runs in to bowl the first ball. Here we go...
NEW ZEALAND (PLAYING XI) - Jeet Raval, Tom Latham, Kane Williamson (C), Ross Taylor, Henry Nicholls, Colin de Grandhomme, BJ Watling (WK), Mitchell Santner, Tim Southee, Neil Wagner, Trent Boult.
ENGLAND (PLAYING XI) - Rory Burns, Dominic Sibley, Joe Denly, Joe Root (C), Ben Stokes, Ollie Pope, Jos Buttler (WK), Sam Curran, Jofra Archer, Jack Leach, Stuart Broad.
TOSS - Up goes the coin and it lands in the favor of the visitors. ENGLAND OPT TO BAT FIRST!

So which side is the favourite heading into this game? New Zealand right? Well, keeping England's record in mind in recent times Down Under and also, how the Kiwis have performed, especially at home, you have to call them the favourites. England however, will surely have a say about that. An exciting 5 days (If the Test goes that long) await! Stay tuned for further updates.

A warm welcome to the coverage of the first Test of this 2-match Test series between New Zealand and England. Not sure how many people from Asia, apart from us will be enjoying this game but surely loads of people from other parts of the world will do so, especially after the enthralling T20I series. The longer format promises to be no less with the first game being played at Mount Maunganui which is hosting its first ever Test match.
